project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to assist Tahoe Forest Products, LLC (TFP), a privately held S-Corporation based in Carson City, Nevada. TFP is engaged in the production of sustainably sourced lumber products. The company began rough lumber operations in May 2024 initially focusing on rough lumber manufacturing using high-altitude red fir, pine, and cedar logs, which make up 98% of its raw material supply. This project which is located in Carson City, Nevada on land leased from the Washoe Tribe of Nevada & California, is to expand to add value-added processing capabilities, including kilns, a planer mill, and a new saw line. This expansion will allow TFP to shift from raw material production to finished lumber suitable for sale to retail distributors and large-scale construction markets. TFP s current capacity is approximately 35,000MBF/year of purely rough lumber, however, with the addition of the new planer mill, kilns and saw line planned capacity will grow to approximately 95,000 MBF/year of premium lumber. This project will add 30 full time jobs to TFP. The TPEP and B&I guarantee loans will both be used to purchase and install equipment; purchase inventory; and help cover associated fees.

The NFTC is a 28-bed residential co-occurring mental health and substance use treatment facility. The demand for residential treatment beds in this area is growing as more judicial (family or specialty) courts are being assigned and diverting offenders to the facility for treatment. The NFTC offers services including psychiatric, primary health, medication management, medication assisted treatment, mental health, co-occurring and substance use treatment, psychosocial rehabilitation, basic skills training, targeted case management and peer recovery support services. This funding will help increase NFTCs capacity from 28 to 42 beds to serve mental health and substance use patients in the community and increase opportunity for recovery.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase a mobile health clinic for the Fallon Paiute Shoshone Tribe (FPST) in Nevada. The clinic will be equipped with a pharmacy dispensing machine and telehealth video equipment to support rural healthcare. The FPST has an agreement with two other tribes in the area to provide health care to tribal members. Without a mobile clinic, medical staff would make weekly trips in multiple vehicles covering 112 miles to provide service to members of the Lovelock Tribe. Providers traveled 230 miles round trip to treat patients of the Yomba Tribe. During the COVID-19 pandemic, medical staff and tribal members would wait outside, often in extreme weather conditions, to provide essential COVID vaccines and treatment. This mobile health clinic will offer accessible care options, including COVID-19 vaccinations, boosters, and healthcare education for staff and for tribal members in all three locations.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to deploy a fiber-to-the-premises network. This network will connect 4,884 people, 130 businesses, 22 farms and seven public schools to high-speed internet in Pershing County. Uprise LLC will offer subscribers symmetrical service tiers of 200 megabits per second (Mbps) or one gigabit per second. naics_industry_sector: Other or Not Defined
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to support the Nevada Health Center as it provides healthcare assistance to underserved populations, rural and border communities, and those living in communities at high risk for infectious disease, hospitalization, and mortality. Nevada Health Center will use funds to serve the rural population of the Amargosa Valley as they address ongoing and immediate needs related to the COVID-19 pandemic. Many rural Nevada counties are experiencing elevated COVID-19 risk due to lagging vaccination rates, higher case counts, and hospitalizations. With limited number of medical facilities in Amargosa Valley, high rates of chronic diseases may increase the severity of COVID-19 infections. This initiative will help sustain and prepare for future pandemic events; increase access to quality health care services, including continued testing and vaccination capability; attainment of medical supplies and equipment to increase medical surge capacity, and recovery of loss revenue from the pandemic impact.

funding_code: INTERMEDIARY RELENDING PROGRAM
naics_industry_sector: Finance and Insurance
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to re-capitalize funding for the Rural Nevada Development Corporation (RNDC), the only intermediary lender in Nevada. RNDC serves 14 rural counties and 27 Native American Tribes. Funds are used to assist small business that cannot obtain conventional credit. The need in the rural areas is significant and the program is well received. Although the number of jobs created or retained and number of people benefiting from this funding remains to be determined, this IRP lender provided more than $6.75 million in loans to small rural Nevada businesses between 1993 and 2018, thereby creating or retaining more than 1400 jobs. Additional funding sources included the applicant, Nevada State Bank, Charles Schwab Bank, First National Bank of Ely and Wells Fargo Bank.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: USDA Rural Development funds will be used to replace pumping equipment and other necessary repairs to restore Well #4, the main water source for the Town of Mina in Mineral County, population 155. The well failed in October 2018 due to damage from numerous small earthquakes in the area; as a result the water supply was reduced 50%. By restoring Well # 4 the citizens of Mina will receive adequate drinking water and an adequate supply of water to maintain the public health of the community without water restrictions. The median household income for Mina is $8,875.
